title: Carats vs Karats: Diamonds and Gold Purity
h1: Carats vs karats — one is mass, one is purity
description: A 2-carat diamond weighs 0.4 g. A 14-karat gold ring is 58.3% pure. Same word, different meaning. Here is the disambiguation.

hero: Carats measure diamond mass. Karats measure gold purity out of 24. The spelling differs in the US and merges everywhere else.
body: Both words come from the Greek 'keration', the carob seed used historically as a small counterweight. The two modern meanings diverged in medieval trade — one for gem mass, one for gold purity — and English preserved both. Confusingly, most of the world spells both 'carat'.

> Diamond carat (ct) = 200 mg = 0.2 g exactly
> Gold karat (US) / carat (UK): fraction of 24
> 24k = 99.9% pure gold (999 fineness)
> 22k = 91.67%
> 18k = 75.0%
> 14k = 58.33%
> 10k = 41.67% (US legal minimum for 'gold')
> 9k = 37.5% (UK legal minimum)

A 1 ct round diamond is about 6.5 mm across. A 2 ct is 8.2 mm — only 26% wider despite doubling the mass, because volume scales with the cube of diameter. This is why per-carat pricing is not linear: a 2 ct diamond is typically 3–4× the price of a 1 ct of the same quality.

Rose gold: copper alloy. White gold: nickel or palladium alloy, often rhodium-plated. Green gold: silver alloy. All can be sold at any karat mark, because karat rates only the gold content — the balance can be any base metal, subject to hallmarking rules.
## Worked example — a 14k gold ring, 5 grams

5 g × 58.33% = 2.917 g of pure gold = 0.0938 troy oz. At a gold spot price of $2,300/troy oz, the gold content is worth $215.70. Retail price will include workmanship, retailer margin, and any diamond content — often 3–10× the raw gold value.
Carat (ct) = 0.2 g of diamond. Karat (k) = /24 of gold purity. The words look alike; the units are unrelated.

faqs.a: The 'metric carat' was standardised in 1907. Before that, carats varied from 188 to 213 mg regionally.
Practically yes — 99.9%. True 100% pure gold does not exist commercially; it is too soft to work and always contains trace impurities.
No — platinum uses parts-per-thousand marks (Pt950 = 95% pure). Karat is a gold-only convention.
